Match the paint handling, palette and mustard-yellow plywood background of the attached reference sheet, but paint four NEW characters; do not copy the reference faces, costumes or props.
A 2x2 grid sheet: four separate square panels separated by thick off-white gutters. Each panel holds one head-and-shoulders portrait, the character centered and facing slightly toward the viewer, the whole head visible with a clear margin around it. Every panel background is the same flat mustard-yellow painted plywood.
Tone: B-movie comedy. Expressions pushed to theatrical exaggeration, adult proportions.
Top-left: Liu Bei, a gentle middle-aged lord with comically long earlobes hanging down to his shoulders, thin black beard, simple jade-green scholar robe and plain cloth cap, big tears streaming down his cheeks, lip trembling.
Top-right: Zhao Yun, a young handsome general in polished silver-white armor and a white cape, a spear held upright beside his face, an overconfident grin showing perfect teeth.
Bottom-left: Zhuge Liang, a calm strategist in a cream Daoist robe and a black silk ribbon scarf cap, holding a white crane-feather fan in front of his chest, eyes half closed with a smug knowing smile.
Bottom-right: Ma Chao, a fierce young western warrior wearing a lion-head helmet and silver scale armor with a white fur collar, teeth clenched, glaring sideways.
